Releasing is a single step: push a git tag on `main` named `vYYYY.MM.N`, for example `v2026.09.2`. The `N` is the release's sequence number within that month. CI then builds the artifacts, runs the full test suite and publishes the release. Don't publish packages by hand.

```
git checkout main && git pull
git tag v2026.10.1
git push origin v2026.10.1
```

This comes from a shared project memory, not from anything in the repo. The `Makefile` and any CI config don't mention release, tag or publish steps, so I couldn't check the process against a pipeline definition. The tag format and the "CI publishes" part rest on that note alone.

I also don't know how to find the next `N` for a month. Run `git tag --list 'v2026.10.*'` to see which numbers are already taken.
